detail:
StatPearls' orthostasis chapter explains that standing shifts blood toward the legs, and the autonomic nervous system normally compensates within seconds. Orthostatic hypotension is diagnosed when that compensation fails: a sustained fall of at least 20 mm Hg systolic or at least 10 mm Hg diastolic within 3 minutes of standing or tilt, measured after at least 5 minutes lying down, with checks at 1 and 3 minutes.

Causes range from dehydration, blood loss, and blood-pressure or other medicines to autonomic failure itself, which clinicians call neurogenic orthostatic hypotension. Evaluation typically combines the orthostatic measurements with a medication review and selected blood tests, because telling the neurogenic form from other causes changes how it is managed.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor if standing regularly makes you lightheaded or faint.
summary: StatPearls defines orthostatic hypotension as a sustained drop of at least 20 mm Hg systolic or 10 mm Hg diastolic within 3 minutes of standing, after lying down for at least 5 minutes.
takeaways: the definition is a 20/10 mm hg drop within 3 minutes of standing
symptoms include lightheadedness, blurred vision, and fainting
causes range from dehydration and medicines to autonomic failure
ask your doctor to check lying and standing blood pressures
title: Orthostatic hypotension: the standing blood pressure drop
